        CimBar (Color Icon Matrix Barcode) encodes binary data into a grid
        of colored geometric symbols. This tool uses a simplified variant:
        each cell encodes 6 bits —
        2 bits select one of 4 colors, 4 bits select one of 16 tile shapes.
        Before encoding, your file can optionally be encrypted with
        AES-256-GCM,
        and each frame's data is protected by
        Reed-Solomon error correction
        (64 ECC bytes per 255-byte block, RS(255, 191), up to 32 byte errors per block).
        Type a message in the Encode tab's Text mode and the receiver sees it as text, ready to copy or save.
      


      

        

          
01

          
Encrypt

          
AES-256-GCM via WebCrypto. PBKDF2 key derivation, 150k iterations, random salt + IV per file.

        

        

          
02

          
ECC

          
Reed-Solomon RS(255, 191) applied to each 255-byte block: 64 ECC bytes, correcting up to 32 byte errors per block.

        

        

          
03

          
Map

          
ECC'd bytes mapped to cells: 2 bits → color (4) + 4 bits → tile (16) = 6 bits per cell.

        

        

          
04

          
Animate

          
Frames rendered to Canvas and compiled into GIF89a using a built-in pure-JS LZW encoder.

        

        

          
05

          
Transmit

          
Share the GIF publicly. Without the passphrase the data is fully opaque.

        

        

          
06

          
Private

          
100% client-side. All crypto and encoding runs in your browser. No server, no storage, no analytics.

        

      


      


      

        Capacity example (608×608 frame):

        One 608×608 px frame is a 64×64 grid of 8 px tiles (1 px gaps) with four 7×7-cell finders.
        3 840 usable cells × 6 bits = 2 880 raw bytes.
        After RS(255,191): 2 112 protected bytes; minus an 8-byte frame header = 2 104 file bytes per frame.
        A 50 KB file needs ≈ 25 frames.
      


      
      

        CimBar web v0.12.1 · build dev
      


      

        GIF palette: The GIF palette holds the four v2 colors plus black and white exactly,
        so encoding is lossless; Reed-Solomon is there for damage and camera errors, not quantization.
